title: Cost of Care Ceiling, Partial Months and Payment in Full for Medical Assistance Residents
content:
Four standing terms of Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Coverage protect the resident against being charged more than the program allows. They apply identically on every tier, from Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Care, Standard Patient Pay through Medical Assistance Hospice Room and Board.

| Term | Setting on every tier |
|---|---|
| A month's patient pay may never exceed that month's cost of care at the Medicaid daily rate | yes |
| Patient pay in a month of admission, discharge or death | the lesser of the patient pay and the days in the center multiplied by the Medicaid daily rate |
| The Medicaid payment plus patient pay is accepted as payment in full for covered days (42 CFR 447.15) | yes |
| A Medicaid resident may be charged for items and services the Medicaid per diem covers | no |

**What the terms mean together.**

- *Cost-of-care ceiling.* Patient pay is the resident's share of the cost of care; it is never set above what the month's care costs at the Medicaid daily rate.
- *Partial months.* In a month of admission, discharge or death, patient pay is the lesser of two figures: the monthly patient pay, and the days in the center multiplied by the Medicaid daily rate.
- *Payment in full.* For covered days, the Medicaid payment together with patient pay is the whole of what the center receives; the resident is never charged for items or services the Medicaid per diem covers.

*Hypothetical partial-month figure:* a resident with a monthly patient pay of 1,486.30 dollars who is in the center for 4 days of a month, on a case whose Medicaid daily rate is 262.15 dollars, has days in the center costing 1,048.60 dollars (4 multiplied by 262.15); the lesser of the two figures, 1,048.60 dollars, is the patient pay for that month.
